method: Every pixel is placed by rule in draw.py. Nothing was generated, cut, traced or retouched. The grammar — row structure, outline weight, the overhang, the plaster cycle, the window and door construction — was measured pixel by pixel off assets/reference/gen2/new-bark-town-gsc.png at 1:1; the colours, the roof hues and the cross-gable are ours.

extraPieces.roof-left / roof-right: roof body carrying the silhouette's side keyline
extraPieces.ridge-left / ridge-right: the crest row at the roof's own edge
extraPieces.wall-left / wall-right: the bottom wall course's corner post and stud
extraPieces.wall-mid: an UPPER wall course, no foundation — see wallCourses below
extraPieces.wall-mid-window: a window on the upper course, where the reference puts it
extraPieces.wall-mid-left / wall-mid-right: the upper course's corner post and stud

hueRamp: hi (crest) > field > rib > shade (eave only). Four swatches each.
ribStep: The field-to-rib step is deliberately small. A large step is what turns a ribbed roof into corrugated sheeting, which is the exact read this family exists to replace. Structure comes from the crest row, the eave, the ridge and the outline — not from the ribs.
outline: c00 #040308 on every face of the silhouette EXCEPT the bottom: the reference has no bottom keyline, it has a foundation lip standing on the ground, and copying the lip is what stops the house looking pasted on.
wallCourses: compose.py spends every row above the eave on roof. The layouts in tools/mapgen/layouts/ author footprints 6 and 7 cells tall, so that rule produces 64px of unbroken roof — a barn. street.py gives anything 5 or more cells tall a SECOND wall course, which is what the reference's own big house does: windows on the upper course, door on the lower.
compatOverlay: built-compat/ carries the thirteen names compose.py loads today. It is SINGLE-HUE on purpose: compose.py's one shared eave list cannot follow a per-house roof hue, and a red roof over a green eave is worse than one good green house. It is an overlay on the existing built/ family, not a replacement — fence-1..3 are not this arm's to draw.
integrationNeeded: To use the four hues and the corner pieces, compose.py's plan_buildings needs to report a cell's COLUMN role (left / interior / right) alongside its row role, and choose the hue once per footprint from the anchor. street.py::Scene.house is a working reference implementation of both.
text: none, on any tile, at any size
determinism: FNV-1a over the footprint anchor decides hue, door column, window columns, ridge row and gable cell. No Math.random, no random module, no clock. verify.py redraws everything and byte-compares (G11).
